task_1.title: Fix RuntimeError for unittest tests on Python 3.12 by adding addDuration support
task_1.description: Python 3.12 introduced an addDuration API to unittest test results. When pytest runs unittest tests on Python 3.12, the runtime attempts to call addDuration on pytest's TestCaseFunction, which lacks that method. This triggers a deprecation warning, and when running with warnings-as-errors (-We), it escalates to a RuntimeError that breaks the test run. The fix adds the addDuration method to TestCaseFunction so it conforms to the updated Python 3.12 unittest TestResult protocol.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that running unittest-based tests via pytest on Python 3.12+ does not raise a RuntimeError ('TestResult has no addDuration method'). Ensure that the TestCaseFunction class conforms to the Python 3.12 unittest TestResult protocol by supporting the addDuration method. Ensure that running with warnings-as-errors mode (-We) does not cause test failures due to missing addDuration support.

expectation.grounded: TestCaseFunction must implement an addDuration(testcase, elapsed) method that satisfies the Python 3.12 unittest TestResult protocol. When Python 3.12's unittest runner invokes addDuration on a pytest TestResult, no warning or RuntimeError should be raised. The method should accept the call silently without affecting existing test duration tracking behavior.
expectation.conceptual: When pytest is used as the test runner for unittest test cases on Python 3.12 or later, the test run should complete without errors or warnings related to missing test result protocol methods. The fix should maintain full backward compatibility with earlier Python versions while adding forward compatibility with the new Python 3.12 unittest protocol.

constraints.grounded: The addDuration method on TestCaseFunction must not alter any existing test timing, reporting, or result behavior. No existing unittest integration methods (addError, addFailure, addSuccess, addSkip, addExpectedFailure, addUnexpectedSuccess, stopTest) should be modified. The method signature must conform to the CPython 3.12 TestResult.addDuration protocol (accepting a test case and an elapsed float).
constraints.conceptual: Existing unittest test behavior and results must remain unchanged across all supported Python versions. The change must be purely additive and non-breaking. No existing test output, duration reporting, or failure handling should be affected by adding the new protocol method.

behavior: TestCaseFunction now implements the addDuration method expected by Python 3.12's unittest framework.
When unittest's test runner calls addDuration on a pytest TestResult in Python 3.12+, the call succeeds silently instead of triggering a missing-method warning.
Running unittest tests via pytest with -We (warnings as errors) on Python 3.12 no longer raises RuntimeError.
On Python versions prior to 3.12, the presence of the addDuration method has no observable effect since the method is never called by older unittest runners.
acceptance_criteria: When running unittest tests via pytest on Python 3.12+, no RuntimeError mentioning 'addDuration' is raised.
When running unittest tests via pytest on Python 3.12+ with the -We flag (warnings as errors), the test run completes without errors related to addDuration.
When running unittest tests via pytest on Python versions prior to 3.12, behavior is identical to the previous version with no regressions.
Given a unittest.TestCase executed by pytest on Python 3.12, when the unittest runner invokes addDuration on the test result, then the call is accepted without warning or error.
Existing test duration reporting and test result output remain unchanged across all Python versions.

task_2.title: Fix shutil.rmtree deprecation warning on Python 3.12 for tmp_path
task_2.description: On Python 3.12, the shutil.rmtree 'onerror' parameter was deprecated in favor of 'onexc', which also changes the callback signature from receiving an exc_info tuple to receiving the exception instance directly. Pytest's internal rm_rf function used the deprecated 'onerror' parameter unconditionally, causing a DeprecationWarning when using the tmp_path fixture. When users configure warnings-as-errors (e.g., filterwarnings = error), this deprecation warning becomes a hard failure, breaking any test that relies on temporary path cleanup. The fix adapts both the rmtree invocation and the error-handling callback to support both the old tuple-based and new exception-based callback conventions, selecting the appropriate parameter based on the Python version at runtime.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the tmp_path fixture does not emit a DeprecationWarning from shutil.rmtree on Python 3.12 and later. Ensure that tests using tmp_path do not fail when the project's warning filters treat warnings as errors. Ensure that temporary directory cleanup continues to work correctly on both Python < 3.12 (using the onerror callback convention) and Python >= 3.12 (using the onexc callback convention).

expectation.grounded: The rm_rf function must call shutil.rmtree with the 'onexc' parameter on Python >= 3.12 and with the 'onerror' parameter on earlier versions. The on_rm_rf_error callback must accept both a bare BaseException (as passed by the onexc protocol) and a classic (Type, BaseException, TracebackType) tuple (as passed by the onerror protocol), and dispatch its error-handling logic (FileNotFoundError suppression, PermissionError handling, PytestWarning emission) correctly in either case.
expectation.conceptual: Temporary path cleanup during test teardown must not produce any deprecation warnings on any supported Python version. The error-handling behavior during cleanup—silently ignoring already-removed files, attempting to fix read-only permission issues, and warning on unexpected errors—must remain identical regardless of which Python version is running.

constraints.grounded: The on_rm_rf_error callback must continue to return False for FileNotFoundError, attempt permission fixes and return True on success for PermissionError, and emit a PytestWarning for all other exception types. PytestWarning messages must include the failing function name, the path, and the exception type and value. Behavior on Python versions below 3.12 must remain unchanged (onerror protocol with tuple-based exc_info).
constraints.conceptual: Existing error-handling semantics during temporary directory removal must not regress. Tests relying on tmp_path must continue to pass on all supported Python versions without any new warnings. The fix must not break compatibility with older Python versions that only support the onerror convention.

behavior: On Python >= 3.12, shutil.rmtree is called with the 'onexc' keyword argument instead of 'onerror', eliminating the DeprecationWarning.

The error callback now accepts either a bare BaseException (onexc convention) or an (exc_type, exc_value, traceback) tuple (onerror convention), and normalizes to a single exception instance for internal handling.
FileNotFoundError during cleanup is silently ignored (returns False) regardless of Python version or callback convention.
PermissionError during cleanup triggers a read-only permission fix attempt, consistent with prior behavior.
Unhandled exception types during cleanup emit a PytestWarning with the exception type and value, using type(exc) and the exception instance directly rather than unpacking from a tuple.
acceptance_criteria: When running tests that use the tmp_path fixture on Python 3.12+, no DeprecationWarning about shutil.rmtree 'onerror' is emitted.
When running tests that use the tmp_path fixture on Python 3.12+ with warnings configured as errors (filterwarnings = error), tests do not fail due to rmtree-related deprecation warnings.
When a file is removed by another process during tmp_path cleanup (FileNotFoundError), cleanup completes silently without warnings on both Python < 3.12 and >= 3.12.
When a read-only file is encountered during tmp_path cleanup (PermissionError), the callback attempts to fix permissions and retry, consistent with prior behavior on all supported Python versions.
When an unexpected error occurs during tmp_path cleanup, a PytestWarning is emitted containing the error type and message, on all supported Python versions.
When running tests that use the tmp_path fixture on Python < 3.12, behavior is unchanged and shutil.rmtree is called with the 'onerror' parameter.

task_4.title: Fix INTERNALERROR IndexError crash when all traceback entries are hidden
task_4.description: In pytest 7.3.0, a change to handle __tracebackhide__ for chained exceptions introduced a regression: when all traceback entries in an exception chain are hidden (e.g., by plugins like hypothesis or pytest-bdd using __tracebackhide__), the exception representation chain could become empty, causing an IndexError crash in ExceptionChainRepr. The 7.3.1 fix reverts that behavior so that getcrashentry() always returns a valid traceback entry (falling back to the last entry even if hidden), ensuring exception display never crashes due to an empty representation chain.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest does not crash with INTERNALERROR IndexError when displaying exceptions where all traceback entries are marked as hidden via __tracebackhide__. Previously in 7.3.0, when plugins or test code caused every traceback entry in a chained exception to be hidden, pytest would produce an INTERNALERROR instead of displaying the test failure. This was observed with plugins such as hypothesis and pytest-bdd that make heavy use of __tracebackhide__.

expectation.grounded: Traceback.getcrashentry() must always return a TracebackEntry (non-optional). When all entries are hidden, it must fall back to returning the last traceback entry rather than returning None. ExceptionInfo._getreprcrash() must always return a ReprFileLocation (non-optional). The repr_chain list passed to ExceptionChainRepr must never be empty; every exception in a chain must contribute an entry to repr_chain regardless of whether its traceback entries are all hidden. ReprExceptionInfo.reprcrash must be typed as non-optional ReprFileLocation.
expectation.conceptual: When a test fails and the resulting exception has all of its traceback entries hidden via __tracebackhide__, pytest must still produce a valid failure report rather than crashing. The crash entry lookup must always succeed by falling back to the last available traceback entry. Exception chain representation must always contain at least one entry so that the failure can be displayed to the user.

constraints.grounded: The fix must not break normal __tracebackhide__ filtering behavior for exceptions where only some entries are hidden; those entries should still be hidden in output as before. The repr_excinfo method must still append entries to repr_chain for all code paths (both when a real traceback exists and when falling back to native repr). The 'value' style must still set reprcrash to None. The skip-exception path in TestReport.from_item_and_call must not raise ValueError for missing crash repr since _getreprcrash() is now guaranteed to return a value.
constraints.conceptual: Normal traceback hiding behavior must be preserved for the common case where only some entries are hidden. The fix must not alter the displayed output for exceptions that have at least one visible traceback entry. Skip handling must continue to work correctly. Exception chain display must remain functional for all combinations of hidden and visible entries across chained exceptions.

behavior: When all traceback entries are hidden via __tracebackhide__, Traceback.getcrashentry() returns the last traceback entry as a fallback instead of returning None
ExceptionInfo._getreprcrash() unconditionally returns a ReprFileLocation without a None guard, since getcrashentry() always yields a valid entry
In FormattedExcinfo.repr_excinfo(), every exception in the chain always appends an entry to repr_chain, preventing the list from being empty when passed to ExceptionChainRepr
The reprcrash value is set to None only when style is 'value', not when all entries are hidden
The None check and ValueError raise for skip exceptions in TestReport.from_item_and_call is removed since _getreprcrash() always returns a valid value
ReprExceptionInfo.reprcrash is typed as non-optional ReprFileLocation
acceptance_criteria: When a test raises an exception where every traceback entry has __tracebackhide__ set to True, pytest should display a failure report without crashing, showing the last traceback entry as the crash location
When a chained exception (with __cause__ or __context__) has all entries hidden in one or more links of the chain, pytest should display the full exception chain without an INTERNALERROR
When using plugins like hypothesis or pytest-bdd that extensively use __tracebackhide__, test failures should produce normal failure output rather than INTERNALERROR IndexError
When only some traceback entries are hidden via __tracebackhide__, the output should remain unchanged from prior behavior (hidden entries are still filtered out)
When a test is skipped, TestReport.from_item_and_call should produce the skip report without raising ValueError
ExceptionChainRepr should never receive an empty repr_chain list

task_3.title: Fix tmp_path performance regression by deferring dead symlink cleanup to session end
task_3.description: In pytest 7.3.0, the introduction of the tmp_path_retention_policy feature caused a severe performance regression, particularly on Windows. Dead symlink cleanup was being performed after every individual test that used the tmp_path fixture, resulting in repeated filesystem traversals of the base temporary directory. This caused near-quadratic overhead as the number of tests grew, with observed slowdowns of up to 2x on Windows CI environments. The fix moves dead symlink cleanup from the per-test tmp_path fixture teardown to the pytest_sessionfinish hook, so it runs only once at the end of the entire test session.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the tmp_path fixture does not cause a performance regression when used with the tmp_path_retention_policy feature. In pytest 7.3.0, test suites using tmp_path experienced significant slowdowns (up to 2x on Windows) due to redundant per-test filesystem cleanup operations. The dead symlink cleanup in the base temporary directory must not be performed after every individual test, but instead deferred to a single pass at the end of the test session.

expectation.grounded: The cleanup_dead_symlinks function must be invoked exactly once per session inside the pytest_sessionfinish hook, not during each tmp_path fixture teardown. The tmp_path fixture's finalizer must no longer call cleanup_dead_symlinks on the basetemp directory. The pytest_sessionfinish hook should call cleanup_dead_symlinks on basetemp only when basetemp is an existing directory. When the retention policy is 'failed' and all tests pass, the basetemp directory should be removed via rmtree before dead symlink cleanup is attempted, and dead symlink cleanup should only proceed if basetemp still exists as a directory afterward.
expectation.conceptual: Dead symlink cleanup in the temporary directory must happen once at session end rather than after every test. The tmp_path fixture teardown must not perform any base directory cleanup. Session-end cleanup must gracefully handle the case where the base temporary directory has already been removed due to retention policy settings.

constraints.grounded: Dead symlinks must still be cleaned up by the end of a pytest session — the cleanup is deferred, not removed. The cleanup_dead_symlinks function must only be called when basetemp is confirmed to be an existing directory via is_dir(). The tmp_path_retention_policy behavior for removing the basetemp directory when policy is 'failed' and all tests pass must remain intact. The rmtree call for basetemp removal must use is_dir() rather than exists() to correctly handle the case where basetemp is itself a dangling symlink.
constraints.conceptual: All dead symlinks must still be cleaned up by session end — no symlink leak is acceptable. The retention policy behavior that removes the entire base temporary directory on a fully passing session must not be disrupted. Directory existence checks must correctly distinguish real directories from dangling symlinks.

behavior: The tmp_path fixture finalizer no longer triggers dead symlink cleanup on the base temporary directory after each test completes.
Dead symlink cleanup is performed exactly once during pytest_sessionfinish, after all tests have completed.
When tmp_path_retention_policy is 'failed' and all tests pass, the basetemp directory is removed first; dead symlink cleanup only runs if basetemp still exists as a directory afterward.
Directory existence is checked with is_dir() instead of exists(), ensuring dangling symlinks are not mistakenly treated as existing directories.
The overall time complexity of dead symlink cleanup is reduced from O(n * m) where n is the number of tests and m is the number of entries in basetemp, to O(m) for a single pass at session end.
The cleanup function is renamed from cleanup_dead_symlink to cleanup_dead_symlinks to reflect that it processes multiple symlinks.
acceptance_criteria: When running a test suite with many tests using tmp_path, the total time spent on dead symlink cleanup should be proportional to the number of entries in basetemp, not the number of tests.
When a test session completes, all dead symlinks in basetemp should be removed, verifying that deferred cleanup still occurs.
When tmp_path_retention_policy is 'failed' and all tests pass, the basetemp directory should be fully removed and no dead symlink cleanup error should occur.
When tmp_path_retention_policy is 'failed' and some tests fail, the basetemp directory should be retained and dead symlinks within it should be cleaned up at session end.
When running on Windows with a large test suite using tmp_path, no significant performance regression compared to pytest 7.2.x should be observed.
Given a test session where tmp_path is used by hundreds of tests, when the session ends, then cleanup_dead_symlinks should be called at most once on the basetemp directory.
